title: Colour-block rectangle wrap
subtitle: A bold two-colour rectangle in aran weight, first half in colour A and second half in colour B
excerpt: This rectangular wrap measures 180 cm wide by 55 cm deep in aran weight yarn. The first half of the rows is worked in colour A and the second half in colour B, creating a bold horizontal colour block across the full width. The stitch is plain treble throughout on a 5 mm hook. The colour join runs along one long edge. Suitable for crocheters who know the treble stitch.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Colour-block rectangle construction is a widely used technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A rectangular crochet wrap in two bold contrasting colours, one on the top half and one on the lower half, draped symmetrically across a person's shoulders, photographed from the front in natural light showing the clean horizontal colour join.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 tr x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran yarn with a 5 mm hook, measured unstretched.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approximately 180 cm wide x 55 cm deep, after blocking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A single horizontal line where two yarn colours meet in a project. In this wrap the join is made by completing the last treble of the final colour-A row with colour B, then continuing all subsequent rows in colour B.

content.text: This wrap divides cleanly across its depth: the first 22 rows are worked in colour A, then the yarn changes at the start of row 23 and the remaining 22 rows are worked in colour B. The
colour-block join
sits at the centre of the wrap's depth, running straight across the full 180 cm width. The stitch is plain treble throughout on a 5 mm hook in aran weight yarn, producing a firm, warm fabric.

The wrap is worked from one short end to the other (the foundation chain sets the 180 cm width; the rows build the 55 cm depth). The ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble on every row. Fasten off colour A at the colour join and join colour B cleanly; there is no need to carry the unused colour.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Colour A: approximately 300 g aran-weight yarn. Colour B: approximately 300 g aran-weight yarn. A 5 mm crochet hook (US H/8). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. Optional: blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge

14 tr x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran yarn with a 5 mm hook, measured unstretched. Swatch in both colours and check they match: colour differences rarely affect tension in the same yarn base, but different dye batches of the same base can vary slightly. A tension difference of even one stitch per 10 cm shifts the finished width by about 13 cm.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern

The wrap is worked flat in rows. The ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble on every row. Do not work into the top of the turning chain on the following row: skip it and work the final stitch of each row into the top of the turning chain from the row below.
Foundation chain, colour A
Ch 255. (This becomes 252 trebles after Row 1, giving 180 cm at the stated gauge.)
Row 1 (right side), colour A
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in the 4th ch from hook. 1 tr in each remaining ch. Turn. (252 sts)
Rows 2 to 22, colour A
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across, working the final tr into the top of the turning ch. Turn. (252 sts)
Colour join

At the end of Row 22, complete the final treble until 2 loops remain on the hook. Draw colour B through both loops to complete the stitch. Fasten off colour A leaving a 15 cm tail. Continue with colour B.
Rows 23 to 44, colour B
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across, working the final tr into the top of the turning ch. Turn. (252 sts)
After Row 44 the wrap measures approximately 180 x 55 cm. Fasten off.

attrs.title: Keeping the join line straight
attrs.body: The colour join will be most visible from the right side. For the cleanest line, complete the final tr of colour A until 2 loops remain, then pull through with colour B as described. Avoid knotting the two colours together at the join, as this creates a bump on the wrong side.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends, including the colour-join tails. Thread the colour-A tail along the underside of the join row for several centimetres; do the same with the colour-B tail in the opposite direction. Wet-block by soaking in cool water, pressing out moisture, and pinning to 180 x 55 cm on a blocking mat.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry. Check the colour join tails after the first few washes.
What to try next

Divide the depth into thirds for a three-colour block: work 15 rows each in three colours. Add a narrow border of double crochet in a third colour around all four edges to frame the colour blocks. Work the same construction in DK on a 4 mm hook for a lighter, longer wrap.
